decisions.difference: A: (active_condition Indigestion)  vs  B: (diagnosis Indigestion probable) [measure task]
decisions.reason: The page measures for GORD once "Dyspepsia (heartburn) likely"; the gold standard triggers follow-on tasks with active_condition, which also covers a definite diagnosis.

decisions.difference: A: Delivery finding  vs  B: Postpartum state
decisions.reason: The page says "Recent delivery": Postpartum state is the state after a recent delivery and is in the shared vocabulary; Delivery finding is any finding about a delivery.

decisions.difference: A: Miscarriage, Induced termination of pregnancy  vs  B: the same with qualifier Recent
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Miscarriage" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value"))) ; same for Induced termination of pregnancy
decisions.reason: The page says "Recent delivery/miscarriage/termination of pregnancy"; B keeps the word "Recent".

decisions.difference: A: Pain radiating to lumbar region of back + thoracic left + thoracic right  vs  B: lumbar only
decisions.final_expr: (or (Pain radiating to lumbar region of back) (Pain radiating to thoracic region left side) (Pain radiating to thoracic region right side))
decisions.reason: The page says "spreading to back", which is not limited to the lumbar region.

decisions.difference: A: Vaginal discharge  vs  B: Vaginal discharge problem (B narrower)
decisions.reason: The page says "abnormal vaginal discharge"; Vaginal discharge problem is the abnormal subtype, while Vaginal discharge includes physiological discharge.

decisions.difference: A: Menstrual cramp  vs  B: Abdominal colic at Lower abdomen structure, During menstruation
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Abdominal colic" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Lower abdomen structure" "body structure")) (qualifier (snomed_concept "During menstruation" "qualifier value")))
decisions.reason: The page says "crampy lower abdominal pain only during periods"; B keeps cramp, lower abdomen and during periods, Menstrual cramp drops the site.

decisions.difference: A: dyspepsia = Postprandial epigastric pain or Hunger pain  vs  B: Postprandial epigastric pain, or Epigastric pain with (Hunger pain or Pain aggravated by position)
decisions.final_expr: (or (Epigastric pain + Postprandial) (and (Epigastric pain) (or (Hunger pain) (Pain aggravated by position))))
decisions.reason: The page asks for "epigastric pain which is worse with eating, hunger or lying down/bending forward"; B keeps epigastric pain in every branch and encodes the positional part that A dropped (Pain aggravated by position is broader than lying/bending, noted).

decisions.difference: A: Obstipation (onset >= 24 h)  vs  B: Obstipation and Unable to break wind (each onset >= 24 h)
decisions.final_expr: (and (>= (onset Obstipation) (time_ago 24 hours)) (>= (onset Unable to break wind) (time_ago 24 hours)))
decisions.reason: "No stools or flatus/wind for past 24 hours" names flatus separately; B encodes both (read as neither stools nor flatus). Whether either alone suffices is not settled by the page.

decisions.difference: A: Appendicitis, Cholecystitis, Pancreatitis  vs  B: Acute appendicitis, Acute cholecystitis, Acute pancreatitis (B narrower)
decisions.final_expr: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Appendicitis" "disorder") probable) ; Cholecystitis ; Pancreatitis, and active_condition of each in the Urgent rule
decisions.reason: The page says "appendicitis/cholecystitis/pancreatitis likely" without "acute"; with descendant matching the Urgent rule's active_condition still fires on Acute forms diagnosed elsewhere.

decisions.difference: A: Infectious disease, evidence inlined in the Urgent rule  vs  B: Female pelvic inflammatory disease, active_condition in the Urgent rule (B narrower)
decisions.final_expr: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Infectious disease" "disorder") probable); Urgent rule: (and (or guarding rigidity) (>= temperature 38) (Vaginal discharge problem))
decisions.reason: The page says only "infection likely"; PID is an interpretation, and inlining the evidence avoids any infection elsewhere making abdominal pain urgent. Which infection is meant is not settled by the page.
The page's ">= 80cm (woman) or >= 94cm (man)" cannot be split by sex; A's or is logically the same as >= 80, so B's single comparison is the honest form.
Rule descriptions taken from B, except the appendicitis/cholecystitis/pancreatitis/infection rules, renamed to match the chosen concepts.

notes: Both builds passed. Base B (more of its encodings were closer to the page). Taken from A: active_condition trigger for the measure task, back radiation including thoracic concepts, the plain diagnosis concepts (Appendicitis/Cholecystitis/Pancreatitis), and Infectious disease for 'infection likely' with its evidence inlined in the Urgent rule. Flowchart from B with rule names updated; remaining questions merged from both. 163 conditions after merge.
